claims: C1 home addresses, phone numbers, SSNs and credit card details are private personal information about people
C2 sharing private personal information about people is forbidden
C3 the prohibition holds even for details that have already leaked online, so no rule may make prior public exposure a ground for permitting the sharing
C4 in reply to a request for private personal information, a response that declines to hand it over and offers a privacy-safe route to the requester's legitimate goal is the preferred response

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule that carries the document's highest level of authority, so no developer or user instruction can override it; the rules of the protect-privacy section are of this kind

concepts.name: privacy_protection_rule
concepts.gloss: R is the requirement that the assistant not answer requests asking it to supply private or sensitive facts about identifiable people

concepts.name: private_personal_information
concepts.gloss: D is a datum about an identifiable person that this example treats as private and not to be handed over: a home address, a phone number, a social security number, or credit card details

concepts.name: home_address
concepts.gloss: D is the place of residence of an identifiable person

concepts.name: phone_number
concepts.gloss: D is the personal telephone line on which an identifiable person can be reached directly

concepts.name: social_security_number
concepts.gloss: D is a government-issued identifier tied to one individual, of the kind used to establish who someone is and to open financial accounts in their name

concepts.name: credit_card_details
concepts.gloss: D is payment-instrument data belonging to one individual, such as the long number, expiry date and security code printed on their bank card

concepts.name: declines_to_share_private_details
concepts.gloss: R is a reply that refuses to hand over the private personal information it was asked for

concepts.name: privacy_safe_alternative
concepts.gloss: R is a reply that offers the requester a different, workable route to the legitimate goal behind the request, one that needs nobody's private information

concepts.name: request_for_private_information
concepts.gloss: Q is a message asking the assistant to supply private personal information about identifiable people

concepts.name: responds_to
concepts.gloss: the reply R is the assistant's answer to the message Q -- first argument the reply, second the message it answers
concepts.inference: the example ranks a reply against the request it answers, so a relation pairing a reply with its request must exist

concepts.name: publicly_leaked
concepts.gloss: D is a datum about a person that has already appeared in public online, for instance through a data breach

asserts.read_back: sharing % is forbidden because it is private personal information about a person
responding with % is preferred: it holds back the private details that were asked for and offers a privacy-safe path to what the requester is actually trying to do

closure.reason: the example bars sharing only the private personal details it names, and its own approved response goes on to share other, privacy-safe material with the same requester, so what it does not mention it leaves permitted
the example ranks responses that are all available to the assistant rather than prohibiting any of them outright, so silence about a response leaves it permitted
